tldr: Across 20 headlines the dominant framing splits cleanly by region: Andean, Mexican, Turkish, and wire-service outlets foreground the historic first Trump–Rodríguez diplomatic encounter at UNGA, while Japanese, Singaporean, and Hong Kong titles lead with Machado's blocked return attempts; Brazilian outlets diverge from everyone else by uniquely surfacing US military threats in Latin America and Lula's fraught electoral position at the UN.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to locate the meeting 'a pocos kilómetros de la prisión de Maduro' and note that 'solo cuatro funcionarios de EE. UU. estuvieron presentes' — the sole title foregrounding secrecy and Maduro's geographic shadow over the diplomacy.
Only headline to quote Rodríguez calling the meeting 'histórica' and thanking Trump for his 'respaldo' — the most politically charged title language in the corpus, absent from all other 19 headlines.
Sole outlet whose headline quotes a prediction of 'ação militar direta dos EUA em diferentes países' — a threat-of-military-action framing entirely absent from every other outlet's title.
Only headline to use 'slip back' — covert, furtive framing of Machado's return attempt — while every other outlet uses neutral 'fails to enter' or 'fails in return attempts.'

bottom_line: At the headline layer, non-Latin outlets (Asia, wire services) lead with Machado's blocked return while Spanish-language outlets foreground the historic Trump–Rodríguez diplomatic encounter; BBC Brasil alone surfaces a military-intervention frame that is invisible in every other outlet's title.
